title: What gradient really means: rise over run
examples: How do you find the gradient of a line?
What does a 10 percent road sign mean?

marks.label: Across 8, up 4
marks.ask: Why is the gradient the same all along a straight line?

explain.say: Think of walking up a ramp. Some ramps are gentle, some are steep. Gradient is a number that tells you how steep. Look at the line starting at the bottom of the board.

draw.text: What gradient really means: rise over run

marks.label: Across 8, up 4
marks.ask: Why is the gradient the same all along a straight line?

explain.say: At this mark you have gone 4 metres across and 2 metres up. Gradient is the rise divided by the run, up divided by across. 2 divided by 4 is one half. Can you say it in words?

marks.label: Across 8, up 4
marks.ask: Why is the gradient the same all along a straight line?

explain.say: For every 1 metre across, you go half a metre up. Now look further along: 8 across and 4 up. 4 divided by 8 is still one half. On a straight line, the gradient is the same everywhere.

marks.label: Across 8, up 4
marks.ask: Why is the gradient the same all along a straight line?

explain.say: Look at these real slopes. A wheelchair ramp often rises just 1 metre for every 12 across, so it is gentle. A road sign saying 10 percent means 10 metres up for 100 across. Which bar is the steepest?

items.label: Road 1 in 10
items.ask: What does a 10 percent road sign mean?

explain.say: Yes, the stairs! Well done. If a line goes down as you move right, like this one, its gradient is negative. Wow: engineers use gradient to design every road, roof and slide. Challenge: a hill rises 3 metres over 6 across. What is its gradient?

marks.label: Going downhill
marks.ask: What does a negative gradient mean?

faq.a: Gradient tells you how steep a line is. It is the rise divided by the run: how far up for each step across.
asks: How do you find the gradient of a line?

faq.q: Why is the gradient the same all along a straight line?
faq.a: A straight line climbs the same amount for every step across. 2 up for 4 across and 4 up for 8 across both give one half.
asks: Does a straight line have one gradient?

faq.q: What does a negative gradient mean?
faq.a: The line goes down as you move to the right. A gradient of minus 2 drops 2 for every 1 across.

faq.q: What does a 10 percent road sign mean?
faq.a: The road rises or falls 10 metres for every 100 metres across. That is a gradient of 0.1.
asks: What does a road gradient percentage mean?

faq.q: What is the gradient of 3 up for 6 across?
faq.a: 3 divided by 6 is one half, so the gradient is 0.5.
asks: Gradient of a hill rising 3 over 6

facts: Gradient = rise ÷ run, the change in y divided by the change in x.
Many building rules, including in the UK and USA, limit wheelchair ramps to about 1 in 12.

quiz.say: A line goes 6 up for every 2 across. What is its gradient?
quiz.why: Rise divided by run is 6 divided by 2, which is 3.

wrong.2: One third divides run by rise, the wrong way round.

quiz.why: A gradient of 4 climbs 4 for every 1 across, the steepest of these.

wrong.1: 0.5 climbs only half a step for each step across.
wrong.2: 1 climbs one step for each step across, less than 4.
